notes.text: Warren Foegele is on injured reserve (knee injury) and has missed the last 10 games.

William Eklund is out 10-12 weeks and has missed the last 19 games. Tim Stützle has taken his spot beside Fabian Zetterlund and Dylan Cozens. That line has had 67% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 71:33 together.
Brandon Hagel is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Zemgus Girgensons is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and missed their last game. Anthony Cirelli has taken his spot beside Pontus Holmberg and Ilya Mikheyev.
Sam O'Reilly was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside Yanni Gourde and Gage Goncalves.
John Carlson is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 22 games, down from 47% with his old team last season.

faceoff.text: Anthony Cirelli is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 29% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 40 seconds at a time, against 78 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Brandon Hagel (6 of 10 changes).

stakes: The Senators go in third in the Atlantic with 31 points, a point behind the Lightning, tied for first. A regulation win for the Senators would lift them past the Lightning.

TBL.head: Leaning the Lightning’s way
TBL.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Even though Tampa Bay will be without Hagel, the Lightning have home-ice advantage. The Senators can still swing it if their penalty kill holds up.

story.head: A measuring-stick game
paras: The Lightning have won two in a row, while the Senators (14-6-3) lost 6-5 in overtime to Philadelphia on Nov 19. Two good teams meet. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Senators third (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Lightning first (tied for fourth). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Senators’ record (.674) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.603), largely because they’re 7-3 in one-goal games. The Lightning’s record (.727) is about what their chances are worth.

The Senators forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd), rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and get into a lot of chippy games (3rd). On the other side, the Lightning ice the puck less than almost anyone (2nd), keep shots away from their net (3rd) and draw more penalties than they take (4th). Tampa Bay has scored 3.73 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Bolts’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Senators.

Tim Stützle (11 G / 17 A / 28 P in 23 GP) leads the Senators in scoring, and Drake Batherson (12 G / 10 A / 22 P in 23 GP) has a team-high twelve goals. Nikita Kucherov (9 G / 22 A / 31 P in 22 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring and is eighth in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. Jake Guentzel (13 G / 14 A / 27 P in 22 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, tied for seventh in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games.
Linus Ullmark (10-1-0 / .940 SV% in 11 GS) has been outstanding for Ottawa and will likely start. Andrei Vasilevskiy (11-5-1 / .895 SV% in 17 GS) is in line to start for Tampa Bay.
At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Gourde, O'Reilly and Goncalves out against opponents’ third lines, so watch for them against Tomasino, Pinto and Batherson.

items.text: The Senators have been without Warren Foegele, Jonas Johansson and William Eklund for several games. Linus Ullmark is expected to start.
The Lightning are newly without Brandon Hagel and Zemgus Girgensons.
Dylan Cozens has six goals in nine games against Tampa Bay since 2023-24, most of them with Buffalo.
Fabian Zetterlund has two goals on chances worth about 5.4 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
